Lana went to join the open battle, while the Commander, Senya, and Arcann proceeded to confront Vaylin at the Alliance base, where the Commander was able to land a killing blow on the Empress, though at the cost of one Alliance member's life. Zakuulan forces then surrendered en masse and the battle was over, but the war was not, as with the Eternal Throne empty the GEMINI captains had gone rogue, bombarding the capital worlds of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Dromund Kaas, and Zakuul into rubble. With claiming the Eternal Throne the only way to stop the destruction, the Alliance leadership departed for Zakuul on the ''Gravestone''.<ref name="KOTETChapter8" />

===The Eternal Alliance===
====The end of Valkorion====
{{Quote|Empress Vaylin has fallen. In her absence, the Eternal Fleet rampages across known space, threatening to wipe out all life in the galaxy. There's only one way to stop them: we must seize the throne.|Lana Beniko|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Lana_Beniko_after_victory.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana and Theron celebrate the fall of Valkorion.]]
Dropping out of hyperspace, Lana and the rest witnessed the Spire [[Blockade/Legends|blockaded]] by the Eternal Fleet, though Iokath upgrades allowed the ''Gravestone'' to [[Battle of Zakuul|breach it]]. Senya and Arcann volunteered to accompany the Commander, and the three traveled down to surface. Making their way to the Spire, they reached the Eternal Throne room, where the Commander claimed the Throne and pacified the Fleet. Valkorion attempted to take over the Commander's body, but with the help of Arcann and Senya he was defeated once and for all, putting an end to his millennia-long existence.<ref name="KOTETChapter9">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=9}}</ref>

[[File:Lana_Beniko_during_briefing.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko continued briefing the Commander about new threats to the Alliance.]]
The Commander then proclaimed the age of the [[Eternal Alliance]], unifying the [[Eternal Empire military|military]] of Zakuul and the Eternal Fleet with the cause of the Alliance under their leadership. The Eternal Alliance was now one of the strongest galactic powers, and as one of its highest-ranking members, Lana had to contend with new threats from the first hours of its existence. Anti-Alliance uprisings sprung across the galaxy, with Lana identifying and ordering the neutralization of such new threats as Renegade Sith Lords [[Adacin]] and [[Zanisk]],<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=uprising|Inferno}}</ref> former Imperial Intelligence Major [[Korven]],<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=uprising|Fractured}}</ref> and exiled Zakuulan Battalion Commander [[Tassar (Human)|Tassar]].<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=uprising|Landing Party}}</ref>

====Return to Iokath====
{{Quote|The Sith Empire and the Republic. They're on Iokath--and they appear to be fighting for control over the superweapon.|Lana Beniko|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_8.png|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko contacts Theron Shan.]]
When the radiation levels on Iokath had subsided, Beniko personally led an Alliance team to map and claim it for the Alliance. She contacted the Commander and Theron with a status report, which was interrupted by her discovery of Imperial and Republic forces on Iokath, who shot her droid [[C6-X]] and appeared to be fighting for control over a superweapon they'd been alerted about. Lana established a secure area at the [[Fleet Spire]] with the Alliance forces at her disposal and detained two emissaries sent by the Republic and the Empire - [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Elara Dorne]] and Major [[Malavai Quinn]]. The Commander and Theron soon joined her on Iokath, though an unknown interference left the Eternal Fleet, now controlled from Odessen, unable to assist. Beniko welcomed the Commander back to Iokath and let her captives introduce themselves, before joining in a holoconference with Sith Empress Acina and Republic [[Supreme Commander (Republic)|Supreme Commander]] [[Jace Malcom]], Theron's father.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Forgotten World|Iokath}}</ref>

[[File:Lana_Beniko_during_War_on_Iokath.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko welcomes the Commander to Iokath.]]
Both sides had arrived on Iokath looking to claim the superweapon and both pleaded with the Alliance to join forces against the other. Lana followed the Commander in the decision they made and was ordered to guard the base while the Commander and Theron went on the offensive against their new enemy.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Shots Fired|Iokath}}</ref> However, Beniko soon discovered that the ongoing [[War on Iokath]] had been orchestrated by an unknown outside party, which had leaked identical data regarding the superweapon to all three governments, hoping to lure them into the same place at the same time. Since the Eternal Throne's control over the Eternal Fleet could only be sabotaged by an Alliance member, Lana suspected a traitor in their ranks.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Lost Arsenal|Iokath}}</ref> The Commander and Theron moved to prevent the superweapon activation, and though they were unsuccessful and the legendary [[Six Gods]] were awakened, their control over the Eternal Fleet was restored, allowing to push the first of the gods, [[Tyth]], back,<ref name="Showdown">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Showdown on Iokath|Iokath}}</ref> and giving them time to destroy the rest.<ref name="Ops">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=operation|Gods from the Machine}}</ref>

====A traitor close to home====
{{Quote|I don't understand. How did I not see this coming? Was I really that blind?|Lana Beniko|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_on_Umbara.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko on Umbara]]
With no way to narrow down traitor suspects from almost half of Alliance personnel, Lana and Theron started to look for the traitor.<ref name="Showdown" /> Eventually Lana found a trail that led to the shadow-world of [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]], where a transmission with the same encryption as the one from Iokath was detected from a [[Hovertrain/Legends|hovertrain]] with a large stockpile of [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] heading for [[Umbaran capital city/Legends|Umbara's capital city]]. Lana, Theron, and the Commander [[Crisis on Umbara|traveled there and boarded the train]] to intercept and stop the traitor. After fighting through several soldiers and [[Umbaran Shadow Assassin]]s, the three reached the empty cockpit of the train, where Theron revealed himself to be the traitor. He shot at Lana and locked her and the Commander inside the cabin, sabotaging the train to crash while escaping on a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]].<ref name="Crisis">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Crisis on Umbara}}</ref>

[[File:Lana_Beniko_after_Therons_betrayal.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko welcomes Aristocra Saganu to Odessen.]]
Managing to bail before the impact and survive the crash, the Commander and Lana chased Theron on foot, while fending off local wildlife and injured [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] soldiers. They caught up with Theron, but were unable to stop him before his shuttle left Umbara. After destroying an [[Umbaran Spider Tank]] and returning to Odessen empty-handed, the Commander ordered Lana to use every resource at the Alliance's disposal to locate Theron's whereabouts.<ref name="Crisis" /> Their message reached the right ears, and [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Saganu]] of the [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force]] arrived on Odessen to personally meet with Lana and the Commander. Saganu revealed that Theron was being sheltered on the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] world of [[Copero/Legends|Copero]] by the rogue [[Syndic/Legends|Syndic]] [[Zenta]] of [[Inrokini family|House Inrokini]].<ref name="Chiss">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|A Traitor Among the Chiss}}</ref>

[[File:Lana_Beniko_in_the_hangar.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Theron's betrayal made Lana determined to track him down at any cost.]]
To avoid a political conflict, Saganu asked the Alliance to [[Mission to Copero|deal with the traitor]], sending Human [[Ensign/Legends|Ensign]] [[Raina Temple]] with the Commander to keep an eye on [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]] interests. Though Theron escaped again, the Alliance learned that he had joined a group looking for a powerful superweapon. The Copero [[Holomap/Legends|holomap]] that pointed to it was destroyed, but Lana put her best [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] into reassembling it.<ref name="Chiss" /> The Alliance also intercepted a message from Theron to his new masters, revealing that he was now working for the [[Order of Zildrog]].<ref name="Nathema">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Nathema Conspiracy}}</ref>

====Chasing Zildrog====
{{Quote|I recognize this encryption method. We developed it together years ago, on Rishi. Only two people know how to decrypt it. Me... and Theron.|Lana Beniko|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_before_the_mission.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko informs the Commander about the intercepted message.]]
Smugglers working for [[Hylo Visz]] eventually intercepted a message to the Alliance from an [[Abandoned listening post|Abandoned Listening Post]] and Lana joined the Commander to personally investigate it. They discovered that the abandoned station had served as the Order of Zildrog's base of operation for months, and that the Order had been able to watch the Alliance that whole time despite the regular security sweeps on Odessen. Holorecordings revealed that the Order was led by former [[Horizon Guard]] [[Vinn Atrius]], who planned to awaken another [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] from Iokath called [[Zildrog]] and use it against Odessen. 
However, a message entered just before their arrival also revealed a set of coordinates on Nathema, which Lana recognized as coming from Theron due to a unique encryption they had developed together on Rishi, indicating that Theron's true allegiance could still lie with them. 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_on_Nathema.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko reluctantly agrees to work with Theron Shan again.]]
Forced to flee as the self-destruct mechanism was activated and completely obliterated the station, Lana and the Commander returned to Odessen just as the work of restoring the holomap from Copero was finished, revealing a location on Nathema that matched the coordinates left by Theron. To stop the Order's plan and deal with Theron one way or another, the Commander and Lana [[Mission to Nathema (Zildrog)|traveled to Nathema]], where they were shocked to see the once lifeless world overgrown with plant life, with no trace of the unsettling wrongness in the Force it had shown before. After dealing with several [[Nathema Zealot]]s and escaped beasts from the [[Sanitarium]], they reached the coordinates they'd been given, where Theron approached them and revealed himself to be secretly working for the Alliance's interests the whole time. 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_in_Zildrog_chamber.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko inside Zildrog's chamber.]]
Though Lana still did not trust him fully, everyone agreed that the Order should be stopped, and Theron led her and the Commander towards the Emperor's Vault under an ancient [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]], where Zildrog was located. Along the way, Theron apologized to Lana for deceiving her, reminding her of the time she had similarly kept him in the dark on Rishi. Theron led the Commander and Lana to the Emperor's Vault, where Vinn Atrius and [[GEMINI 16]] were already in the process of awakening Zildrog. Theron shot Atrius, but GEMINI 16 trapped the three of them in a [[force field]] and finished summoning Zildrog, allowing it to remotely take over the ''Gravestone'' that remained parked on Odessen.<ref name="Nathema" />

====A blow to the Alliance====
{{Quote|This goes without saying, but... I'm not going anywhere. The Alliance may be different now, but I'm here to stay.|Lana Beniko|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Lana_checks_Therons_injuries.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana checks up on Theron's injuries.]]
Controlling it from the Dark Sanctuary, Zildrog took the ''Gravestone'' into Odessen's orbit and proceeded to repeatedly fire the [[omnicannon]] at the Eternal Fleet, which sat defenseless in the abscence of orders from the Eternal Throne. Hylo Visz contacted the Commander and informed them of the crisis, but they, Lana, and Theron were unable to do anything to stop Zildrog from completely annihilating the Eternal Fleet. It then targeted Odessen itself, but needed to recharge before the next attack, forcing GEMINI 16 to engage the Alliance directly. Lana, Theron, and the Commander destroyed her, and Theron attempted to shut Zildrog down, but was stabbed in the back by Vinn Atrius with a [[Lightsaber pike/Legends|lightsaber pike]]. Atrius then ordered Zildrog to augment him with its power and attacked Lana and the Commander with his new increased strength. They defeated Atrius and destroyed Zildrog, which also caused the self-destruct of the ''Gravestone'' and disabled the Eternal Throne. The Commander decided Atrius' fate while Lana tended to Theron's wounds, determining that he needed to be immediately brought to Odessen for treatment. The Commander agreed and the three of them returned to the base.<ref name="Nathema" />

[[File:Lana_Beniko_after_Nathema_Conspiracy.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko give a report to Commander in the aftermath of Zildrog Crisis.]]
Lana did an assessment of the incident and reported to Commander that although Odessen had suffered minimal damage with no casualties to Alliance personnel, the ''Gravestone'' and the Eternal Fleet, two of Eternal Alliance's greatest weapons, were gone.<ref name="Nathema" /> Without them, the Alliance no longer possessed the military force to rival that of the Republic and the Sith Empire, who were redoubling their preparations for the inevitable renewal of open hostilities. Additionally, many Alliance members were choosing to leave and rejoin their original factions, their goal of toppling the Eternal Empire accomplished.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Alliance Update - State of the Galaxy}}</ref> Lana however assured the Commander of her continued loyalty to them and the Alliance and the two of them welcomed back Theron, who apologized for keeping them in the dark and asked the Commander to allow him back into the Alliance.<ref name="Nathema" />

===New Galactic Conflict===
====Invasion of Ossus====
{{Quote|The Alliance is still a formidable power, but we're not strong enough to face the Republic or the Empire. Unfortunately, a confrontation is inevitable.|Lana Beniko to the Commander|<ref name="KOTET" />}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_offers_faction_choice.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko asks whether Commander would support the Republic or the Empire.]]
In the year [[3628 BBY]],<ref name="TOR Dates Forums">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=9852711#edit9852711|text=Charles Boyd on Forums: "Dear Story Team, What Year Are We Currently In?" (1)}}</ref> Lana Beniko met with the [[Alliance Commander]], and informed them that with a new war on the horizon, what was left of the Alliance needed to pick a side. Ultimately, the Commander chose to side with the Galactic Republic, and Lana set up a meeting between them and an agent of the [[Republic Strategic Information Service|SIS]] named [[Jonas Balkar]].<ref name="TOR510">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Inflection Point|Odessen}}</ref>

Later, when a [[Third Galactic War|new conflict]] between the Sith Empire and Republic erupted with an [[Invasion of Ossus|invasion]] of a [[Jedi Colony]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], the Commander joined the Republic's side in aiding and defending the colony. Lana remained behind on Odessen, as the mission called for the Commander to head in alone.<ref name="TOR510" />

The [[3627 BBY|following year]],<ref name="TOR Dates Forums" /> Lana Beniko held a meeting between the Commander and the various leaders of the Alliance, including [[Juvard Illip Oggurobb|Doctor Oggurobb]], [[Hylo Visz]], [[Bey'wan Aygo]], [[Theron Shan]], and [[Koth Vortena]]. During the meeting, Beniko informed the Commander of three Imperial spies who had each tried to infiltrate the Alliance since their formal alignment with the Republic. As the meeting concluded, Lana mentioned to the Commander that a news reporter for a [[Republic News Network]] by the name of [[Alec Ranin]] had attempted to get in contact with the Commander for an interview.<ref name="HeartsAndMinds">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|Hearts and Minds|Odessen}}</ref>

====Mission to Onderon====
{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_on_Onderon.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko on Onderon]]
Later in the year, when the Commander was tasked with heading to [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]] with [[Arn Peralun]] in order to ensure the safety of the [[Eleventh Fleet (Galactic Republic)|Republic fleet]] refueling in orbit, Lana made sure to arrive ahead of the Commander and learn about the Imperial's plans. During Lana's meeting with the Commander and Arn, she jokingly taunted Arn, commenting that she rarely got to menace young [[Padawan/Legends|padawans]] anymore.

She explained the situation on Onderon to the Commander, speaking about how the political environment was a powder keg with [[King/Legends|King]] [[Regalun Petryph|Petryph]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Deja Nebet]] having been at odds with each other for months, additionally finding out with the help of [[Theron Shan]] that Petryph intended to strip mine the planet to line his pockets. To add onto that, she had been informed by Nebet's informants that coded transmissions detected to be coming from [[Royal Hunting Lodge|Petryph's hunting lodge]] were not [[Onderonian/Legends|Onderonian]], but Imperial.<ref name="PalaceIntrigue">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Palace Intrigue|Onderon}}</ref>

[[File:Lana_Beniko_and_Jakarro.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko is reunited with Jakarro and C2-D4.]]
Immediately following a sudden attack by the [[Untamed]], Lana informed the Commander that they'd need a guide if they were to continue their mission on Onderon, and re-introduced them to [[Jakarro]] and [[C2-D4]].<ref name="PalaceIntrigue" />

After the Commander was able to capture [[Darth Savik]], Lana and Theron explained that they had loaded her up onto an [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]] [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], and that, while Savik wished to stay with the Alliance Commander, the Republic was requesting for her to be transferred over to their control. They left the decision of who would get Savik up to the Commander.<ref name="SpringingTrap">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Springing the Trap|Onderon}}</ref>

====Mission to Mek-Sha====
Lana, alongside Theron Shan, accompanied the Commander to [[Mek-Sha]] in order to ensure that the [[Twenty-Ninth Fleet]] commanded by [[Vice Admiral/Legends|Vice Admiral]] [[Dol Narlock]] would be able to refuel safely. While the Commander was meeting with Narlock and [[Junker Jott]], Lana and Theron mentioned to [[Hylo Visz]] and [[Gault Rennow]] that they were on Mek-Sha.<ref name="GangsOfMekSha">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|The Gangs of Mek-Sha|Mek-Sha}}</ref>

Following the Empire's assault on Mek-Sha's docks, Lana informed the commander that [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ardinondu Dipolus Daeruun|Daeruun]] had sent coordinates to a strategy meeting on how best to defend Corellia, and had strictly instructed them that only the Commander was to attend.<ref name="DefendingTheDocks">{{TORcite|exp=ons|type=general|Defending the Docks|Mek-Sha}}</ref>

====Defending the Meridian Complex====
[[File:Gnost-Dural_and_Lana_Beniko.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko enjoys a philosophical discussion with Master Gnost-Dural.]]
Lana, along with the Commander and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Gnost-Dural]] rode aboard General Daeruun's personal ship to Corellia. During the flight, Lana and Gnost-Dural discussed philosophy about the Force, and her personal take on it. During that conversation, Lana stated that she'd grown far stronger working alongside the Commander than she ever could have through treachery, which Gnost-Dural said was hardly the Sith approach. He found it intriguing, however, and acquiesed that the [[Code of the Sith/Legends|Sith Code]] never specifically called for the usurption of the master by the apprentice, just the pursuit of greater power. Lana agreed, further stating that it was only natural for the strongest to lead, but that the ultimate goal was power, not necessarily leadership, and that if one was truly strong leadership would inevitably come. When Gnost-Dural claimed her thinking to be a unique point-of-view among the Sith, Lana suggested that perhaps it was why they weren't among the Sith at that moment.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|exp=ons|Objective: Meridian}}</ref>

Once planet-side, Lana was placed in a ground-team alongside [[Aric Jorgan]]. The two headed towards a tram pylon, with Jorgan looking to set up a [[Sniper/Legends|sniper]] perch. Eventually, they spotted a large group of Imperial reinforcements, and moved to head them off. They were backed up by Theron Shan, who told the Commander to keep moving. However, some of the reinforcements got past them, but were intercepted by Gnost-Dural and Daeruun.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian" />

[[File:Lana_Beniko_on_Carrick_Station.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko muses on working with the Republic and the Jedi.]]
Following the defense of the complex, and the transformation of the Alliance into [[Task Force Nova]], Lana and Theron spoke with the Commander aboard [[Carrick Station]]. Lana jokingly commented that she'd need to invest in some brighter clothing, then mentioned that it would take some time for them to be able to properly decorate Odessen to match their new allegiance to the Republic, but she would get things underway as soon as possible. She expressed her thoughts that fitting in with the Republic and the Jedi would be an interesting situation for her, but admitted that Gnost-Dural seemed open-minded enough, to which Theron stated that he'd told her that Gnost-Dural was alright. She mentioned that she'd have to keep her more proactive methods to herself from that point on. Lana then changed the subject, suggesting that she, Theron, and the Commander stop by the cantina, as a general was offering free drinks to anyone with an impressive Corellia story. Before they could, however, [[Tau Idair]] and Arn Peralun took the Commander aside for a brief conversation, to which Theron and Lana obliged before departing.<ref name="ObjectiveMeridian" />

====Tenebrae's Final Weapon====
[[File:Lana_Beniko_after_Echoes_of_Oblivion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana stays with the Commander as they awaken from the ordeal.]]
In [[3626 BBY]],<ref name="Dates6.2">{{TOR_updates|6.2}}</ref> [[T7-O1]] discovered the location of the [[Kira Carsen's ship|vessel]] that [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] and [[Kira Carsen]] had placed [[Satele Shan]] and her students aboard after it had been momentarily lost. The Alliance Commander, alongside Carsen and Scourge, prepared to set out to deal with the situation, as onboard the ship, [[Tenebrae]]'s [[Tenebrae's curse|final weapon]] was getting stronger by the minute. However, just before they departed, Lana stopped the Commander to wish them good luck. She expressed that she was disheartened that she couldn't aid the Commander in facing Tenebrae again, but acknowledged that it was something they must do without her. When [[Theron Shan]], [[Senya Tirall]], and [[Arcann]] all insisted upon joining the Commander, Lana informed them that she'd keep their forces on high alert, and if they were needed she'd rush to assist.

Following Tenebrae's ultimate and final defeat, Lana arrived to pick up the Commander after they briefly passed out. She mentioned that she was able to feel Tenebrae's death, before piloting the Commander away from the ship.<ref name="Echoes of Oblivion">{{TORcite|type=general|exp=ons|Echoes of Oblivion|Odessen}}</ref>

====Conflicting Priorities====
Following the [[Attack on the Spirit of Vengeance II|Attack on the ''Spirit of Vengeance II'']], Lana and Hylo Visz met with the Alliance Commander to discuss the state of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. They briefly mentioned that Task Force Nova was receiving countless requests for aid, and it was draining their resources. Lana then shifted to talking about how since the death of Tenebrae, practically all Force Sensitives across the galaxy felt as if the Force felt lighter, as though Tenebrae's presence was a weight no one had recognized. She suggested keeping the [[Force Enclave]] as well as [[Sana-Rae]] on the lookout, just in case, but expressed hope that Tenebrae was well and truly gone.

[[File:Lana_Beniko_in_Conflicting_Priorities.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko presents Commander her "test" for Zenith.]]
She mentioned to the Commander that [[Jekiah Ordo]] was keeping his promise in aiding the Task Force's operations, and was securing escorts for cargo shipments in [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla's]] place. She moved on to speaking about bringing in extra specialists to help with requests that the Task Force had been receiving, and spoke of a shipment of [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] being produced on [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] for a Republic Base on Corellia. The issue came from the fact that the Sith Empire had discovered the shipment, and was prepared to ambush it. Lana suggested bringing in a Balmorran rebel named [[Zenith]] to protect the shipment. The Commander agreed to the plan, and had [[Bey'wan Aygo]] reach out to Zenith.<ref name="Conflicting Priorities">{{TORcite|type=general|exp=ons|Conflicting Priorities|Odessen}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You're unusual for a Sith. You don't even have a title.''"<br />"''Knowledge, answers, truth, the Force: ''these'' are the things I hold dear. Titles don't interest me.|The Outlander and Lana Beniko|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Lana_Beniko_meditating.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko meditates on her homeworld of Dromund Kaas.]]
Lana Beniko had a very unusual personality for a Sith Lord. She spoke in a very serene and considerate manner, and possessed a keen mind with a preference for analyzing a problem rather than charging in head on. She was a patriot of the Sith Empire and seemed to care more about its safety than her own goals or achieving new titles. She frequently used the saying "May the Force ever serve you (serve you well)" when addressing people she respected. As advisor to Arkous, she felt bad when her suspicions of him turned out to be true,<ref name="FAI" /> and even years later would remember him, wishing that Arkous could see what she had become.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" /> Her patriotism made her pragmatic enough to ally with unlikely individuals against threats to the Empire.<ref name="FAII" /> 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_with_Republic_troopers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|As a Sith Lord, Lana Beniko had no issues working with those loyal to the Republic.]]
Beniko genuinely grew to care for her friends on both sides and would show worry when they were in danger. Unlike many other Sith, Beniko held no disdain for non-Humans, people without Force-sensitivity, and even loyal citizens of the Galactic Republic; neither did she have the urge to remind them of their place. Her outward appearance showed little to no effect of Dark Side corruption apart from yellow eye irises, and she possessed a healthy sense of humor, free from the sadistic tendencies typical of Sith.<ref name="FAIII" /> She was, however, willing to play the part of a stereotypical Sith to unnerve Jedi, admitting to the Commander that she found doing so fun. She easily fit in with unlikely companions for weeks, and it took the combined force of an extremely stressful situation and constant annoyance to get her to even raise her voice in a situation most Sith would choose to settle with either a Force-choke or their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="KOTFEChapter11" /> 

Despite all this, Beniko was able to make hard decisions and remained a loyal Imperial even after she was branded a traitor, and refused an offer to defect to the Republic.<ref name="FAIII" /> Beniko sincerely regretted when Theron lost his trust in her after Rishi, and she parted with him on good terms though she was already prepared to made his life difficult in her new role at Sith Intelligence. Her calm outward demeanor was also contrasted by her prowess in combat, and she had no qualms about using [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] against Revan during the fight.<ref name="The Enemy Within" /> The stress of her new post as [[Minister of Sith Intelligence|Sith Intelligence Minister]] combined with the power Vitiate displayed on Ziost took a toll on Lana, visibly wearing her out. She put her trust in [[Rane Kovach]] and when his betrayal was revealed to her, immediately ordered his death.<ref name="Monolithic" /> 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_7.png|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko worked closely with Theron Shan for many years.]]
Though Theron still mistrusted her, she had no problem working with him to stop Vitiate. She became angry when he refused to let her experiment on Master Surro, though only because she believed sacrificing the Jedi's life could help save the entire galaxy from annihilation by Vitiate.<ref name="Dead Center" /> Despite being a patriot, she abandoned the Sith Empire after the [[Zakuul–Imperial treaty]] and went to search for her old ally in Wild Space, believing from their past efforts that they were the only person capable of stopping Arcann.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" /> She made multiple friends and contacts during her years in Zakuulan space, enough that when called upon quite a few showed up to start the Anti-Zakuulan Alliance.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> 

Lana worked alongside [[Koth Vortena]] for years, growing to genuinely like and trust him.<ref name="KOTFEChapter5" /> Although not violent or cruel by nature, she was prepared to sacrifice the innocent when she believed the fate of the entire galaxy at risk, at evidenced by her desire to experiment on Master Surro<ref name="Dead Center" /> and to let the [[Sun Generator]] on [[Zakuul]] explode to cover their escape. Despite leaving the Sith Empire behind, she still thought of herself as Sith, taunting the Zakuulan Knight [[Tanek]] that the Knights were never taught to properly channel their anger like she was.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" /> After becoming the master of [[HK-55]], Beniko had become quite attached to the bodyguard droid and when [[SCORPIO]] insensitively labeled the HK-series droid inferior, she threatened to deactivate her. Beniko was initially saddened to see HK destroyed during the [[Battle of Asylum]],<ref name="KOTFEChapter8" /> but happily embraced his ultimate reconstruction at the hands of [[Juvard Illip Oggurobb]].<ref name="Interlude" />

[[File:Lana_Beniko_welcomes_Alliance_Commander.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Lana Beniko showed great concern for the safety and wellbeing of the Alliance Commander.]]
In the early days of the Alliance, Lana acted as a voice of reason, trying to settle petty disputes and past grievances, such as those between Koth Vortena and [[Senya Tirall]]<ref name="KOTFEChapter12" /> or between Theron Shan and SCORPIO.<ref name="KOTFEChapter11" /> She was always wary of SCORPIO and showed no sign of sorrow at her supposed death, but was nevertheless unable to foresee the depth of SCORPIO's deception.<ref name="KOTFEChapter15" /> Putting her trust in the Commander, Beniko expected trust in return and did not take lightly to being lied to. Protective of the Commander, she promised to tear the Scion Sanctuary apart should something happen to them<ref name="KOTFEChapter6" /> and was extremely worried when the Commander was trapped in the [[Odessen]] wilderness by Valkorion.<ref name="KOTFEChapter12" /> 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_betrayed_by_Theron_Shan.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lana was deeply stung by Theron's betrayal on Umbara.]]
When the Commander took harsh actions against traitors, Lana always stood by their side, even if she had brought the people in question in to begin with.<ref name="KOTETChapter3" /> She tolerated ruthless decisions only if they were pragmatic, and was quick to point out when mindless violence only led to more problems down the line.<ref name="KOTFEChapter15" /> Lana was furious at Theron's supposed betrayal on Umbara and blamed herself for being unable to foresee it, vowing to use all of her efforts to hunt him down and make him pay.<ref name="Crisis" /> Despite this, she was able to overcome her anger and work with him again, after Theron revealed himself to be a double agent who had Alliance interests in mind the whole time.<ref name="Nathema" /> 

[[File:Lana_Beniko_in_the_pilot_seat.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko was an expert pilot.]]
Lana was extremely loyal to her ally from the Revanite crisis who later became the Alliance Commander, spending five years searching for them in Wild Space<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" /> and following them through whatever hardships fell upon them, to the point where she stopped associating herself with the Sith Empire and had no desire to visit her homeworld of Dromund Kaas again, a far cry from her previous devotion.<ref name="Nathema" /> Her daily schedule was strongly regimented and consisted of [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]], sparring practice and coordination of Alliance spy networks. Lana followed a strict diet, which included a mixture of [[Tea/Legends|tea]] and bourbon before sleep, and wrote [[Poet/Legends|poems]] on her personal encrypted [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]].<ref name="parents" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|You need to go. Now. I'll handle the knights."''<br />''"There's too many of them, you'll be overwhelmed."''<br />''"Don't insult me.|Lana Beniko and the Outlander|<ref name="KOTFE" />}}
[[File:Lana_Vaylin.png|thumb|right|250px|Lana Beniko uses Force lightning against Empress Valyin.]]
Despite her calm and serene appearance, Lana was a fully-trained Sith Lord of great wisdom and strength.<ref name="codex" /> She was proficient with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and frequently employed both [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]] and [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] against her opponents.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" /> Lana had a strong affinity with the Force, which allowed her to sense the threat of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] through her connection to [[Darth Arkous]],<ref name="FAI" /> and to discover Odessen, which would serve as the permanent base of the Alliance.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" /> She was a capable leader with a strong strategic mind, which she applied to both military operations and to managing a vast network of agents and spies who answered directly to her.<ref name="KOTETChapter5" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Lana_beniko.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lana Beniko original concept art by [[Chris Anderson (artist)|Chris Anderson]]]]
Lana Beniko is a character in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' voiced by English actress [[Lydia Leonard]]. First appearing as part of the ''Forged Alliances'' storyline in game update 2.7, released in April [[2014]],<ref name="FAI" /> she played a major role in every subsequent expansion and story update, becoming one of the most prominent NPCs in-game. She serves as mission control for the player during the four Forged Alliances flashpoints, the [[Temple of Sacrifice]] operation, three Uprisings introduced in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']], and the [[Odessen]] Proving Grounds warzone.<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Lana becomes a companion for the player in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] expansion, which signifies the five-year time skip by changing her character model, outfit and hairstyle.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" />

She is portrayed as bisexual through romance options for male and female player characters. Players of the Republic and Empire factions have the option to flirt with Lana on several different occasions during the ''Forged Alliances'' storyline,<ref name="FAIII" /> potentially leading to a more developed romance and culminating in a passionate kiss at the end of the ''Shadow of Revan'' expansion.<ref name="The Enemy Within" /> The player can resume the romance or initiate it from clear slate during the ''Knights of the Fallen Empire'' storyline.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" />

Lana remains a critical character throughout [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']], being the Outlander's most frequent companion, being particularly important on [[Nathema]].<ref name="KOTETChapter7" /> In the Light Side path, her prominence diminishes slightly during the last two Chapters as [[Senya Tirall]] and [[Arcann]] accompany the player in the fights against [[Vaylin]] and [[Valkorion]]. However, if the player follows the Dark Side path, both Senya and Arcann die prior to that and their roles are assumed by Lana and Theron, who remain by the player's side throughout the showdown with [[Vaylin]] and during the final push to the Eternal Throne, and will be the ones to broadcast the Outlander's ascension on the HoloNet.<ref name="KOTETChapter9" />

===Gameplay alternatives===
[[File:Lana_Beniko_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''Fallen Empire'' concept of Lana Beniko]]
*During the ''Legacy of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata'']] flashpoint, Lana will ask Imperial players to collect data on the [[Infinite Army]] cyborgs for the Empire.<ref name="Legacy of the Rakata">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=flashpoint|Legacy of the Rakata}}</ref> If the player refuses, she will lament that it did not matter, as she is now a fugitive and could not hand over the data anyway.<ref name="FAIII" />

*On [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] the player can force [[Rane Kovach]] to reveal himself as a mole for [[Leontyne Saresh]] and either kill him themselves, let Lana Force-choke him, or order him to flee.<ref name="Monolithic" /> If the player maintains Kovach's identity on Ziost, he can later reveal it to Lana on [[Vaiken Spacedock]] after Ziost is destroyed, undermining her faith in her abilities.<ref name="The End of It All" /> The player can also let Lana take Master [[Surro]] to the Empire for experimenting on her brain, to Theron's disapproval.<ref name="Dead Center" />

*In [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Fallen Empire'']] Chapter III, Lana will insist on leaving the [[Sun Generator]] to explode, killing thousands of Zakuulians. If the player picks this Dark Side option, it will affect their conversations with [[Koth Vortena]] later on. The player can also let Lana kill [[Tanek]], or order her to let him go, in which case [[Vaylin]] executes him for his failure.<ref name="KOTFEChapter3" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter IV, the player can choose whether to tell Lana that [[Tenebrae|Valkorion]] continues to exist in their mind. If the player withholds this information, the truth comes out during Chapter VI, which affects Lana's approval with the Outlander.<ref name="KOTFEChapter4" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter V, the player can choose to use Valkorion's power and save Lana from a seemingly fatal blow by a Zakuulan Knight. In this case, Lana becomes greatly concerned by the display of such power. If the player refuses, she survives with only a minor wound.<ref name="KOTFEChapter5" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter VIII, either Lana or Koth will come to the Outlander's aid during the second fight with Arcann, depending on who is romanced or has higher affection. She is alarmed if the player uses Valkorion's power to defeat Arcann, or saves the player after being stabbed if the offer is refused.<ref name="KOTFEChapter8" />

[[File:Steam_Trading_Cards_Lana_Beniko.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Lana Beniko]]
*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter IX, the player can initiate a romance with either Lana, Theron, or Koth if they have enough [Flirt] options. Should the player later resume their romance with a returning original companion, they will have to break up with Lana.<ref name="KOTFEChapter9" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter X, if the player alienates [[Koth Vortena]] into abandoning the Alliance, Lana will attempt to persuade him to stay.<ref name="KOTFEChapter10" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter XV, Lana will become angry if the player lets [[Zasha Ranken]] die in favor of saving [[Malita Tal]] and [[Tai Cordan]].<ref name="KOTFEChapter15" />

*In ''Fallen Empire'' Chapter XVI, if the player previously alienated Koth Vortena, he will return and steal the ''Gravestone''. Lana will put out a search for him.<ref name="KOTFEChapter16" />

*In [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Eternal Throne'']] Chapter I, the player can remain hostile to Senya Tirall. In this case, instead of providing her cover, Lana and the Mandalorian forces will attack Senya, only for the player to arrive and finish her off.<ref name="KOTETChapter1" />

*In ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter III, if the alienated Koth Vortena tries to make amends, Lana will reply that whatever was between them was over. She will whisper goodbye to Koth if the player decides to kill him.<ref name="KOTETChapter3" />

*In ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter VII, Lana will strongly suggest the player keep [[Dramath]] imprisoned in the holocron. If the player makes this Dark Side choice, the final fight against Vaylin in Chapter IX will be made much easier.<ref name="KOTETChapter7" />

[[File:Theron_Shan_and_Lana_Beniko_in_Eternal_Throne_room.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Theron Shan and Lana Beniko reach the Eternal Throne.]]
*In ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter VIII, if Senya and Arcann were previously killed, Lana will accompany the player all the way through, up to the fight against Vaylin.<ref name="KOTETChapter8" />

*In ''Eternal Throne'' Chapter IX, if Senya and Arcann were previously killed, Lana and Theron will accompany the player to the Eternal Throne. They will then hold off the [[Skytrooper]]s as the player fights Valkorion in their mind, sharing a tender moment when they believe they are making their last stand.<ref name="KOTETChapter9" />

*In ''War for Iokath'' storyline, Lana will voice her opinion on allying with the Sith Empire. Though remains indifferent even if the player joins the Republic<ref name="Iokath">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Forgotten World|Iokath}}</ref>

*At the end of "The Nathema Conspiracy" flashpoint, players can order Lana to abandon Theron to die, in which case Lana will try to protest, but will reluctantly follow orders. If the player has romanced Lana previously, they can propose to [[Marriage/Legends|marry]] her.<ref name="Nathema" />

*In ''Onslaught'', during the mission "Conflicting Priorities", if the player is an Imperial alligned character rather than a Republic one, Lana will instead suggest telling Zenith that the shipment of turbolasers meant for the Republic Base on Corellia is instead meant for the Empire, thus setting him upon it.<ref name="Conflicting Priorities" />

*In ''Legacy of the Sith'', if the player is Imperial, Lana will accompany them and [[Darth Rivix]] to the ruins of the [[Temple of Nul]] on [[Elom (planet)/Legends|Elom]], where they will defeat [[Darth Malgus]] and then participate in his arrest alongside [[Darth Krovos]], [[Darth Xarion]], and either [[Darth Acina|Empress Acina]] or [[Darth Vowrawn|Emperor Vowrawn]] depending on the player’s choices during ''War for Iokath''.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=flashpoint|Ruins of Nul}}</ref>
